title: Which tmuxp syntax one port's workspace loader supports
description: One record per port, written by that port's catalog test from what the test observed loading each example, not by hand. A port's test fails when its checked-in record and what it observes disagree. The features and the examples that exercise them are in syntax-features.json.

port.description: The port's name as the docs site spells it, such as `go`.

surface.description: What was loaded: the command, function or type whose output the test compared with the expected structure.

tmuxp.description: The tmuxp release whose examples and expected structure the test used.

files.description: One entry per example, sorted by file name, as the test saw it.

features.description: One entry per feature in syntax-features.json, in that file's order, derived from `files`.

outcome.description: `matches`: the loaded model equals the expected structure. `deviates`: it loads, and differs in exactly the places `deviations` lists. `refused`: the loader reports an error.

path.description: RFC 6901 pointer into the expected file, or into the port's mapped view where the port's model has no counterpart.

reason.description: Why the port differs, in a sentence a reader of the compatibility table can use.

message.description: The error the loader reports, verbatim.

features.description: The features the refusal is about; the rest of the file was not checked.

status.description: `supported`: an example exercises it and its file matched, and none contradicts. `supported_with_difference`: it loads and a deviation names it. `refused`: a refusal names it. `unverified`: no example that matches exercises it, so the test saw nothing either way.

detail.description: null when supported or unverified. The deviation reasons, or the refusal messages, joined with a semicolon.

files.description: The examples that exercise the feature.
